comparison: Perfect agreement on C21-C26, C60, C72-C73. Both evaluations find the in vivo data showing differential Aff3ir-ORF2 expression under disturbed shear stress to be convincing and well-supported across multiple methodologies.

Disagreement on C27-C30, C32. OpenEval finds the anti-inflammatory effects fully supported with appropriate protein-level validation. Peer reviewers initially rated UNCERTAIN, requesting additional ELISA validation because 'mRNA level and protein level does not always correlate,' though concerns were later addressed.

Agreement on C31-C32 (in vivo atherosclerosis reduction). Both find the overexpression data in atherosclerotic models convincing. Peer review specifically affirms this subset of claims as SUPPORTED while questioning other inflammatory markers.

Perfect agreement on C33-C39, C68. Both evaluations find the global knockout mouse data demonstrating increased atherosclerosis with Aff3ir-ORF2 deficiency to be solid and convincing with appropriate controls.

Disagreement on C40-C47, C62. OpenEval finds the RNA-seq and bioinformatics analyses meet appropriate standards. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, raising detailed methodological concerns about euclidean distance correlation, GO analysis gene selection, q-values, and enrichment methodology, though concerns were eventually addressed.

Agreement on C48-C51, C63, C90 (mechanistic interaction between Aff3ir-ORF2 and Irf5). Both find the subcellular fractionation and functional data showing cytoplasmic retention convincing. OpenEval also includes C78 which peer review addresses separately.
Agreement on C78 specifically. Both evaluations accept the Irf5 translocation data as part of the mechanistic evidence without specific concerns.

Perfect agreement on C52-C55, C64, C79. Both evaluations find the genetic rescue experiment with Irf5 knockdown to be strong evidence for the proposed mechanism, with peer review calling it 'cleverly designed.'

Disagreement on C56-C59, C65, C83. OpenEval finds the AAV-ICAM2 endothelial-specific delivery data supported but notes long-term efficacy remains uncertain. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN due to concerns about 'leaky expression' of the ICAM-2 promoter in non-endothelial cells, questioning cell-type specificity.
Agreement on C1-C5, C66. Both evaluations accept these background claims about atherosclerosis as established knowledge supported by appropriate citations.
Agreement on C6-C10. Both evaluations accept these background claims about mechanosensitive proteins and shear stress as established prior work with appropriate citations.
Agreement on C11-C17. Both evaluations accept these background claims about the IRF family and Irf5 as established literature providing necessary context.
Agreement on C18-C20. Both evaluations accept these claims as prior work from the same research group providing essential background.

Disagreement on C70 (endothelial-specific mechanism). OpenEval finds this inference supported by literature and differential effects on plaque vs collagen. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'other cell types such as smooth muscle cells or macrophages could be contributing' since the knockout is global and other experiments lack cell-type specificity.
Agreement on C69. Both evaluations accept this mechanistic inference about cell-type specificity as reasonable, though peer review questions the strength of evidence elsewhere (see R9).

Agreement on C74. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting it is speculative and untested. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED but acknowledge it is presented as hypothesis rather than definitive claim. Both recognize this as speculation about regulatory mechanisms.
Agreement on C75-C77. Both evaluations accept these as established prior work about Irf5 in atherosclerosis providing important context.
Agreement on C81-C82. Both evaluations accept these as prior therapeutic approaches to Irf5 that provide context for novelty.
Agreement on C80. Both evaluations accept this as prior work on Irf5 therapeutic approaches providing context.
Agreement on C85-C88. Both evaluations accept these as established roles of Irf5 in other diseases providing context for potential future applications.

Agreement on C67, C84, C91 (therapeutic potential). Both evaluations accept these as speculative future directions rather than demonstrated facts. OpenEval notes therapeutic potential 'remains speculative pending further validation.' Peer review acknowledges 'relevance for possible human health interventions' while recognizing these as future directions.
OpenEval includes C61 and C89 in main conclusions as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these summary conclusion claims.
